thread:
Maya: kicking off canary for v2.14.0 to 10% in eu-west now — keeping an eye on kv/cache and tail latency
deploybot: scheduled: shift traffic 10% -> v2.14.0 (canary) — change_window=2026-03-23T09:30Z
Jin: +1 saw a small bump in 95th latency on kv-store in eu-west right after the shift, nothing huge yet but eviction rate doubled
Sam: any 5xx spikes or user-facing errors?
Jin: few 502s from edge (snippet): ```502 upstream connection reset by peer```; not widespread but coincides with canary timing
Priya: linking dashboards — telemetry: https://dash.redwood/telemetry/eu-west/canary-3498765432 and kv evictions graph
Maya: ok let's pause the rollout until we confirm root cause. holding at 10%
Sam: +1 hold. can we pin traffic back to baseline if it worsens?
Maya: deploybot, please prepare a rollback/pin option (soft abort)
deploybot: action available: routing-pin -> route 0% to v2.14.0 (pin/rollback). queued on confirmation
Jin: quick check: samples show heavy prefix churn from a small subset of clients — increased cache churn could explain the evictions
Priya: adding note to release notes draft: "Canary paused due to KV cache churn in eu-west; investigation in progress"
Maya: decision time — propose soft-abort (pin and roll back eu-west only) while we triage. anyone object?
Sam: no objection, prefer safe rollback to avoid customer impact
Jin: i'll keep digging into request patterns and run a KV tune test on a replica env
Maya: ok confirming: deploybot execute routing-pin -> revert eu-west to v2.13.9 (traffic 100% for eu-west)
deploybot: executing: routing-pin -> reverting v2.14.0 -> v2.13.9 for region eu-west; updating traffic: 10% -> 0% for v2.14.0
OpsBot: NOTICE: traffic rollback initiated by Maya — canary v2.14.0 traffic set to 0% in eu-west
Sam: will this change the global rollout plan? we should mark the release as "soft-aborted" pending fixes
Priya: setting status in release tracker: "Canary paused / soft-abort — investigations ongoing (INF-3482)"
Maya: created follow-up ticket INF-3482 assigned to eng-runtime for KV caching investigation
Jin: after rollback, 95th latency back to baseline on quick smoke run; evictions dropped to normal
Sam: good sign. next steps: run kv-tuning in staging, try a synthetic workload resembling the offending client
Priya: adding details to release notes + changelog: include rollback reason and which region was affected
Maya: agree. plan: hold global rollout, fix config or hotfix, re-run canary to 5->20% with KV changes. ETA 2-4 hours for initial perf test
deploybot: NOTE: rollout status changed -> CANARY_SOFT_ABORTED by Maya
Maya: thanks everyone. i'll post another update in this thread once INF-3482 has initial findings :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Incident bot: created INF-3482 (Investigate KV cache churn during canary) and assigned to eng-runtime
Priya: tagging on-call for runtime: @Jin you have the lead, Sam as backup
Jin: got it — starting investigation now, will report back in 30m
Maya: marking thread closed for now (soft-abort). reopen when ready to resume or after fixes :white_check_mark:
